title: Ketogenic diet reduces liver fat by 67% in clinical trial
summary: A ketogenic diet reduced liver fat by 67% in people with obesity and fatty liver disease, significantly outperforming Mediterranean (45% reduction) and low-fat diets in a clinical trial. All three groups lost approximately 10% of body weight over four to five months, with about half of ketogenic par
takeaways: 67% liver fat reduction on ketogenic diet vs. 45% on Mediterranean and low-fat diets
Ketogenic diet: 4% carbs, 73% fat; Mediterranean: 50% carbs, 35% fat; Low-fat: 70% carbs, 15% fat
All groups achieved ~10% body weight loss over 4–5 months
~50% of ketogenic group reversed prediabetes status
Published August 27, 2026, in Cell Metabolism; led by Samuel Klein at Washington University

title: Scientists identify protein C3 as shortcut to calorie restriction's anti-aging benefits
summary: Yale researchers identified complement protein C3 as a driver of age-related inflammation, finding that blocking it in mice reduced inflammation. A study of 42 CALERIE trial participants showed moderate calorie restriction (11–14% reduction) significantly lowered C3 levels, suggesting C3 targeting c
takeaways: C3 is an immune protein driving age-related chronic inflammation
Moderate calorie restriction (11–14% over 2 years) significantly lowered C3
White adipose tissue is primary source of C3 production affected by diet
Blocking C3 in mice reduced age-related inflammation
Research remains early stage; animal studies confirm mechanism

title: Early childhood sugar exposure linked to cancer risk and aging 70 years later
summary: A study of over 64,000 Britons used postwar sugar rationing as a natural experiment to show that reduced sugar exposure during the first 1,000 days of life correlates with lower cancer rates and slower biological aging decades later. Liver cancer rates were approximately 69% lower, and breast cancer
takeaways: Study tracked 64,000+ people born 1951–1956 using sugar rationing as natural experiment
Liver cancer approximately 69% lower with extended early-life rationing
Breast cancer 36% lower with extended early-life rationing
Extended rationing also linked to longer telomeres, indicating slower biological aging
People with longer rationing maintained healthier diets into adulthood around age 50

title: Long-term melatonin use linked to 90% higher heart failure risk
summary: A large preliminary study found chronic insomnia patients using melatonin long-term had approximately 90% higher risk of developing heart failure over five years. The findings raise questions about the long-term safety of the over-the-counter supplement, which lacks FDA regulation for strength and p
takeaways: 90% elevated heart failure risk over 5 years in chronic melatonin users with insomnia
Associations also found with heart failure hospitalization and all-cause mortality
Data from TriNetX Global Research Network covering electronic health records
Study does not establish causation
OTC melatonin supplements lack FDA regulation for potency consistency

title: Ketogenic diet restores exercise benefits for people with high blood sugar, study finds
summary: Researchers at Virginia Tech discovered that a high-fat ketogenic diet can help people with elevated blood sugar regain the ability to benefit from exercise, particularly improved oxygen utilization. In mice with hyperglycemia, the keto diet normalized blood sugar within one week and enhanced muscle
takeaways: Mice fed a ketogenic diet saw blood sugar normalize to non-diabetic levels within one week
The diet caused muscle remodeling, increasing slow-twitch oxidative fibers and aerobic exercise capacity
Study published February 25, 2026 in Nature Communications
Led by exercise medicine researcher Sarah Lessard at Virginia Tech's Fralin Biomedical Research Institute

title: Sucralose and Stevia May Have Multi-Generational Effects on Gut Health
summary: Research shows that the zero-calorie sweeteners sucralose and stevia alter the gut microbiome in mice with effects that may persist across generations.

title: Researchers develop bioavailable spirulina with natural vitamin B12
summary: Researchers produced spirulina containing biologically active vitamin B12 at beef-comparable levels by controlling light conditions during cultivation.

title: Study links ultra-processed foods to 30% higher prostate cancer risk
summary: A nationally representative study of 17,000 U.S. men found that higher consumption of ultra-processed foods was associated with a 30% increase in prostate cancer risk.

title: Genetic predisposition determines low-carb diet's effect on LDL cholesterol
summary: People with genetic susceptibility to high cholesterol experience sharper LDL spikes on low-carb diets high in saturated fat, explaining variable dietary outcomes.

title: Waist Circumference May Better Detect Health Risks Than BMI
summary: A simple waist measurement is nearly as effective as complex methods for detecting unhealthy body fat and may catch obesity cases that BMI misses.

title: Study finds fungal toxins in all 212 plant-based meat alternatives tested
summary: A UK study found that all 212 plant-based meat alternatives examined contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin, though levels remained below EU guideline limits.

title: Sports nutrition market projected to reach $141.3 billion by 2033
summary: The global sports nutrition market is forecast to grow to $141.3 billion by 2033 driven by fitness industry trends.

title: Study: Vitamin C ineffective at preventing colds, minimal impact on symptoms
summary: Research confirms that vitamin C does not prevent most people from catching colds, though regular supplementation may slightly reduce symptom severity.
